text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of doing all the work at once, teams break the project into small parts called "sprints." Each sprint usually lasts one to four weeks and focuses on completing specific tasks. Every day, the team has short meetings called "standups" to discuss progress and any problems. All the work needed for the project is kept in a "backlog," which is a list of tasks or features. These tasks are often written as "user stories," describing what a user needs. With iterative development, the team builds and improves the product gradually, getting feedback after each sprint.
